title: Virtual Legal Assistant of the Rights Mapping and Analysis Platform (RiMAP) to Improve Legal Analysis and Access to Rights and Solutions for Forcibly Displaced and Stateless Persons
summary: UNHCR is building the RiMAP Virtual Legal Assistant to collect, summarize and analyze laws affecting displaced and stateless people; its 30 percent cut in research time is a target.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: In a June 2025 account, UNHCR describes an internal prototype that collects, summarizes and analyzes laws affecting displaced and stateless people. UNHCR set a target to cut preliminary legal research time for targeted tasks by 30 percent within 12 months of full deployment. The account reports that UNHCR staff evaluate the internal prototype and that users rate each output on four criteria. The same account names building the prototype as the next step. No later source reports a released assistant, measured time savings or a public chatbot.
purpose: Help legal advisers maintain and analyze information about displaced people's rights.
location: Intended coverage: legal frameworks across UN countries and territories

ratings.reason: UNHCR editors and legal advisers are intended to save research time. The 30 percent cut is a target for 12 months after full deployment, and no observed gain is reported.
Displaced and stateless people are intended to gain access to legal information through a later public chatbot. No outcome for an individual's rights or services is documented.
More inclusive legal frameworks are an intended downstream benefit. No source records a change in policy.

ai_role.statement: The account does not separately assess AI’s contribution to the benefit.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 11: Virtual Legal Assistant of the Rights Mapping and Analysis Platform (RiMAP) to Improve Legal Analysis and Access to Rights and Solutions for Forcibly Displaced and Stateless Persons
evidence.quote: Target: Aim to reduce preliminary legal research time for targeted tasks by 30% within 12 months of full deployment.

evidence.citation: Renjun Tang and Liudmila Zavolokina, Testing the RiMAP Virtual Legal Assistant: Findings from User Study with UNHCR Staff and Partners, University of Lausanne (IRIS repository), 14 September 2026. Researchers at the University of Lausanne who worked with UNHCR on the assistant report a test on 225 questions and a study with 24 users. They give no dates for either and do not measure research time.
evidence.title: Testing the RiMAP Virtual Legal Assistant: Findings from User Study with UNHCR Staff and Partners
evidence.quote: To prove its readiness for pilot deployment, the VLA underwent rigorous end-to-end evaluation using a benchmark of 225 highly complex questions designed by UNHCR legal experts.

later.note: On 14 September 2026, researchers at the University of Lausanne who helped build the assistant reported tests on 225 questions from UNHCR's legal experts and sessions with 24 staff and outside experts. No participant would rely on it as a final source of legal information, and in three sessions they found citations that did not match the cited text.
later.quote: Our initial results show a consistent trend across all participants: none were willing to treat the VLA as a final source of legal information, yet all recognized its value as a starting point.
